title: CAA raids Kollupitiya supermarket over missing food labels
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has carried out a special inspection raid on a leading supermarket in the Kollupitiya area over the sale of imported packaged food products allegedly lacking mandatory labeling information.

title: High waves expected in several sea areas
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned that rough sea conditions and strong winds are expected in several sea areas around the island during the next 24 hours.

title: Rain and strong winds expected today
byline: The Meteorology Department says showers or thundershowers will occur at times today (14) in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and North-Western provinces, as well as in the Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts.

title: Two wanted crime suspects deported from UAE
byline: Two alleged organized crime figures and drug traffickers wanted by Sri Lankan law enforcement were deported from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and arrived at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake on last Friday night (12).

title: Trump says US-Iran deal to be signed on Sunday as Tehran casts doubt on timing
byline: President Donald Trump has said a deal to end fighting between the US and Iran is scheduled to be signed on Sunday, after Iran cast doubt on the timing.

title: Special programme launched to help healthcare workers curb tobacco use
byline: The Ministry of Health and Mass Media has launched a series of training programmes to equip healthcare workers with psychological intervention techniques aimed at preventing tobacco use and helping users quit smoking.

title: Heavy rain expected as El Niño conditions set to develop globally after February: Officials
byline: Meteorologists have predicted that the El Niño phenomenon, triggered by rising temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean, will begin to have a global impact after February next year, with increased rainfall patterns expected in several regions.

title: “LTTE diaspora will not fund Government again, will not vote to bring it back,” Says MP Archchuna
byline: Jaffna District Parliamentarian Ramanathan Archchuna has alleged that the LTTE diaspora, which he claimed had previously supported the government, will no longer provide financial backing or vote to return it to power.

title: Wild elephant, calf electrocuted in Okkampitiya
byline: A wild elephant and a calf have died after getting entangled in an electric wire set up illegally at a farmland in the Jothi Amuna area of Maligawila, Okkampitiya.

title: Funeral for Iran’s late Supreme Leader Khamenei to begin July 4, burial set for July 9
byline: The funeral for Iran’s late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei will begin in Tehran on July 4 and ​conclude with his burial in his hometown, the northeastern holy city of Mashhad, ‌on July 9, state media reported on Saturday.

title: Scotland hang on for first World Cup win since 1990 with 1-0 victory over Haiti
byline: Scotland, roared on by their Tartan Army of travelling fans, savoured ​their first World Cup win in 36 years on Saturday when they edged past Haiti for a scrappy 1-0 victory settled ‌by a first-half strike from John McGinn.

title: Shanaka, Mishara star as Sri Lanka draw T20 series against West Indies
byline: Sri Lanka produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat the West Indies by 37 runs in the second T20 International, leveling the two-match series 1-1.

title: Court allows Tissa to seek answers from Prime Minister
byline: The Colombo District Court on Friday (12) permitted Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) National Organiser Tissa Attanayake to serve interrogatories on Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, seeking answers regarding her educational background and her knowledge of the destruction allegedly caused by the JVP during the 1987–1989 insurrection, in connection with the defamation lawsuit filed by the Prime Minister against him.

title: Modified Dengue strain driving surge in cases: Health Ministry
byline: A modified strain of the dengue virus is contributing to the current spread of the disease in Sri Lanka, increasing the risk of infection among the population, Deputy Minister of Health Hansaka Wijemuni said.

title: Over 5,000 Bharatanatyam dancers in Colombo clinch Guinness World record
byline: A historic cultural milestone was achieved in Colombo today as more than 5,000 Bharatanatyam dancers performed together, clinching the Guinness World Record for the largest Bharatanatyam dance lesson. The event, organised by Sangamam Global Academy, India and Samgamizh Liya, Sri Lanka, was held at Galle Face Green in Colombo and brought together thousands of dancers from Sri Lanka,

title: Hamilton wins first grand prix for Ferrari as Antonelli retires
byline: An emotional Lewis Hamilton took his first victory for Ferrari in a compelling Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix as championship leader Kimi Antonelli retired from second place with four laps to go.

title: Refugee-Turned-Star Irankunda delivers
byline: Irankunda creates football history at the World Cup as breaking news continues to emerge from the tournament.
